facts.text: On this date in 1871, the Great Chicago Fire began — but a fire the same night in Peshtigo, Wisconsin killed roughly 2,500 people, making it the deadliest wildfire in U.S. history. Almost nobody remembers it.

On this date in 1967, Che Guevara was captured in Bolivia. He was executed the next day, aged 39, having never successfully exported revolution to a single country despite becoming the world's most printed face.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Dhaka, Bangladesh than live outside it. That single region contains over half of all humanity.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined — roughly 879,000 of them, holding about 20% of the world's fresh surface water.
The city of Chongqing, China, is administered as a single municipality but covers an area larger than Austria, with a population exceeding 32 million — more than Australia's entire country.
On this day in 1987, markets were eerily calm — just nine days before Black Monday wiped 22% from the Dow in a single session, the largest single-day percentage crash in Wall Street history.
On October 8, 1929, the Dow hit what analysts called a 'permanently high plateau.' Within three weeks, it had lost a third of its value.
The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant it once had a market cap equivalent to roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Class A share has never been split. A single share costs over $700,000, making it the highest-priced stock on any major US exchange.
The London Stock Exchange was founded in a coffee house. Jonathan's Coffee House on Exchange Alley was where brokers met to trade shares in the 1690s before formalizing in 1801.
On this date in 1604, Kepler observed a supernova visible in daylight for weeks. We now know its remnant is expanding at 11 million mph — and still accelerating.
On this date in 1871, the Great Chicago Fire ignited. Across the lake that same night, the Peshtigo fire killed ten times more people and is still the deadliest in US history.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Your body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, yet 90% of the DNA inside you belongs to microbes. You are, by gene count, mostly not human.
Light takes 8 minutes to reach Earth from the Sun, but the photons themselves were generated in the solar core up to 100,000 years ago, slowly fighting their way out.

On this day in 1871, the Great Chicago Fire began — the same night a firestorm killed twice as many people 250 miles north in Peshtigo, Wisconsin. History remembers the city; it forgot the 2,500 dead.
On this day in 1967, Che Guevara was captured in Bolivia. He was executed the next morning without trial, aged 39 — younger than most people are when they first read his biography.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, making it older than the telephone by 33 years. Alexander Graham Bell was not yet born when someone successfully transmitted a document over wire.
The University of Oxford began teaching in 1096. When the Aztec Empire was founded in 1428, Oxford had already been educating students for over 300 years.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She and Neil Armstrong are separated by 2,000 years; she and Khufu by 2,500.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. It spread fast because it named something previously nameless.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word meaning a look shared between two people who both want something but won't initiate it. Linguists consider Yaghan, spoken on Tierra del Fuego, functionally extinct — one native speaker remained as of 2022.

On this date in 1871, the Great Chicago Fire began. The city rebuilt so fast that architects invented the skyscraper there within 15 years. The German word for this urgency: Torschlusspanik — gate-closing panic, the fear that time is running out.

On October 8, 1965, the Post Office Tower opened in London. The Finnish word torschlusspanik has a cousin: myötähäpeä, meaning second-hand embarrassment — feeling shame on behalf of someone who feels none themselves.

Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops, also from Koenig's Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows. No ancient root — just a sound that felt old. Sometimes a word earns its place not by age but by precision.

On this date in 2016, The DAO attacker began moving stolen ETH through a child DAO — exploiting the same 30-day lock-up that was meant to protect victims, buying time that ultimately forced Ethereum's contentious hard fork.
On this date in 2021, Coinbase's direct listing had already repriced Bitcoin's institutional legitimacy: its S-1 disclosed 56 million verified users before a single share traded on Nasdaq.
Bitcoin's timelock script opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, was dormant in the codebase for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015 — the original code comment read 'reserved for future use.'

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — a timestamp, a political statement, and proof no coins were premined before that date.
Ethereum's EIP-1559 has permanently burned over 4 million ETH since August 2021, making the network's monetary policy directly sensitive to gas demand — more activity, more deflation.

On this date in 1997, Garry Kasparov formally submitted his protest over Deep Blue's move 36 in Game 2 — a move IBM later confirmed was chosen by a bug, not genius. It may have broken him psychologically anyway.

On this date in 2010, the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge held its second competition. The winning error rate was 28%. Two years later AlexNet would cut that to 16%, triggering the modern deep learning era.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, for a single model trained once.

Transformers were introduced in 2017 with 65 million parameters. Seven years later, frontier models are estimated at one to two trillion. That is a 15,000-fold increase in about the time it takes to finish a PhD.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) was not invented for language models. The core technique was published in 2017 for video game agents, and its authors did not anticipate it would later dominate how chatbots are aligned.
